/repos/jdx/demo/pulls/6519.title: perf(v4): build the safeParse error on first read
/repos/jdx/demo/pulls/6519.body:
Builds `result.error` on first read: a failing `safeParse` spent ~85% of its time finalizing issues and constructing the `ZodError`, which a caller that only branches on `success` never reads. The Standard Schema surface finalizes issues straight off the raw payload, so it never goes through the lazy result.

Measured against `main` (Node 26.7, Apple Silicon, load < 9, best of 4 interleaved rounds):

| | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `safeParse` invalid, only `.success` read | 1057 ns | 336 ns |
| `safeParse` invalid, `.error.issues` read | 1060 ns | 1442 ns |
| `~standard.validate` invalid | 419 ns | 402 ns |
| `safeParse` valid, `.parse()` throw | unchanged | unchanged |
| Every mini bundle | — | +47 B gzipped |

The result is a literal with a getter and a setter, five lines. The alternative — one shared accessor descriptor plus a hidden state slot on each result — reads ~15% faster (273 ns / 1255 ns on the two failing rows) because every result then shares one map and the `.error` load sites stay monomorphic, but it costs ~75 B more gzipped in every bundle; at mini's scale that is the wrong trade, so the getter stays.

Two things to weigh either way:

- Readers pay for the accessor; `error` has to stay own and enumerable (keys, spreads, `structuredClone`, `toEqual`), so a per-result getter is the floor, and `#private` fields would downlevel to WeakMaps under the es2020 target.
- Error maps (`customError`, `localeError`, per-schema maps) run on the first read of `error`, against whatever config is live then, instead of at parse time. The nine tests in `issue-schema.test.ts` that watch the maps through a bare `safeParse` now read the error explicitly. Stack traces are unaffected: a `safeParse` error has had no stack since #6450.

Where it shows: benchmarks that discard the failing result or read only `.success` — the "Invalid data" parsing rows and the invalid-string rows on schemabenchmarks.dev, `packages/bench/error-handling.ts`, and the `.success`-only section of the old zod-compiler comparison (37x → ~10x). The moltar suite calls `.parse()` on valid data only and does not move. Standard Schema rows are already covered by #6509.

An opt-in form (`safeParse(data, { lazyError: true })`) keeps readers and the map timing unchanged but ships the same bytes.

commit.messageHeadline: fix: keep the async rerun when a sync Standard Schema validate meets a promise

nodes.name: Test with TypeScript latest on Node lts/* (ubuntu-latest)

nodes.body:
The async re-run sits outside the `try` and outside any `async` function, so a synchronously-throwing check now escapes `validate()` as a thrown exception. The old path went through `_safeParseAsync`, an `async` arrow, which converted that same throw into a rejected promise — verified both ways against `main`:

```ts
z.string().refine(() => { throw new Error("boom"); })["~standard"].validate("abc");
// main:      returns a promise, rejects with "boom"
// this PR:   throws "boom" synchronously
```

`StandardSchemaV1.Props["validate"]` is typed `Result | Promise<Result>`, and the common consumer shape (`const r = schema["~standard"].validate(v); if (r instanceof Promise) r = await r;`) doesn't wrap that first call, so this surfaces as an uncaught exception downstream. Neither `classic/tests/standard-schema.test.ts` nor the mini equivalent covers a sync-throwing check — they only exercise `.refine(async …)`.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# `~standard.validate` can throw synchronously

## Affected sites
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts:346-350` — `catch (_) {}` swallows the sync attempt's throw, then the unguarded `inst._zod.run({ value, issues: [] }, actx)` on line 348 re-throws it out of `validate()`. A schema that throws deterministically throws under both contexts, so the second run reproduces the first.
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/parse.ts:103` (on `main`) — `_safeParseAsync` was `async`, which is what previously turned the sync throw into a rejection.
- `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/schemas.ts:282-289` — classic spreads `core.standardProps(this)` verbatim, so it inherits this.

## Required outcome
- Once `validate` has committed to the async branch, every failure from that branch surfaces as a rejected promise, never a synchronous throw.
- A test in `classic/tests/standard-schema.test.ts` pinning a synchronously-throwing `.refine()` / `.check()` through `~standard`, asserting a rejection rather than a throw. It has to fail on the current commit.

## Suggested approach (optional)
Bring the second `run` back under a promise boundary, e.g. an `async` IIFE or `Promise.resolve().then(...)`, and weigh the bytes against the three mini fixtures the same way the getter-vs-descriptor choice was weighed.
````

</details>
